check_connection.title: Check the connection
check_connection.description: List the project's visible event types with this week's totals, uniques and percent of DAU. The cheapest real call on the Dashboard REST API, so it doubles as a credential check; list_event_types gives the tracking-plan view with categories and descriptions instead.

output.description: Visible events, each with value (raw name), display name, totals, hidden, deleted and non_active flags.

list_events.title: List events with weekly totals
list_events.description: List every visible event type in the project with this week's totals, uniques and % DAU, as shown in the dashboard's event picker. Hidden events are left out. Use the value field as event_type in segmentation, funnel and retention queries.

output.description: Visible events, each with value (raw name), display name, totals, hidden, deleted and non_active flags.

get_chart_results.title: Get a saved chart's results
get_chart_results.description: Get the results of any saved chart by its chart id (the part after /chart/ in the chart's URL). The response shape depends on the chart type. The quickest way to read a chart someone already built; use the segmentation, funnel and retention tools to query ad hoc.

chart_id.description: The chart id from the chart's URL, e.g. abc123 in https://app.amplitude.com/analytics/demo/chart/abc123.

output.description: The chart's results; the shape varies with the chart type.

get_active_users.title: Get active or new user counts
get_active_users.description: Count active or new users per day, week or month over a date range, optionally segmented and grouped by a property. Returns one series per group.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

interval.description: 1 for daily, 7 for weekly or 30 for monthly counts (default 1).

segments.description: Segment definitions as a JSON array string, e.g. [{"prop":"country","op":"is","values":["United States"]}]. Each element has prop, op (is, is not, contains, does not contain, less, less or equal, greater, greater or equal, set is, set is not) and values; use prop "userdata_cohort" with a cohort id to segment by a cohort. Custom user properties are prefixed gp:.

group_by.description: Property to group by, e.g. country, platform or gp:utm_campaign for a custom user property. Only with a single segment.

output.description: The chart data: data.series (one array of values per group), data.seriesLabels or seriesMeta, and data.xValues (dates).

get_session_length_distribution.title: Get the session length distribution
get_session_length_distribution.description: Count sessions in each session-length bucket over a date range. Supply bin_min, bin_max and bin_time_unit for custom buckets, and bin_size for a fixed bucket width; otherwise Amplitude picks the buckets.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

bin_min.description: Lower bound of the custom buckets, e.g. 0.

bin_max.description: Upper bound of the custom buckets, e.g. 600.

bin_size.description: Width of each custom bucket, e.g. 60. Without it Amplitude picks the bin size.

output.description: data.series with a count per bucket and data.xValues with the bucket bounds.

get_average_session_length.title: Get average session length
get_average_session_length.description: Get the average session length, in seconds, for each day in a date range.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

output.description: data.series with the daily average session length in seconds, and data.xValues.

get_sessions_per_user.title: Get average sessions per user
get_sessions_per_user.description: Get the average number of sessions per user for each day in a date range.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

output.description: data.series with the daily average sessions per user, and data.xValues.

get_user_composition.title: Get user composition by property
get_user_composition.description: Get how users are distributed across the values of one user property over a date range, e.g. how many users are on each app version or in each country.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

property.description: The user property: version, country, city, region, DMA, language, platform, os, device, start_version, paying, or gp:<name> for a custom one.

output.description: data.series with unique users per value, data.xValues with the property values.

get_event_segmentation.title: Query event segmentation
get_event_segmentation.description: Run an Event Segmentation query: uniques, totals, % DAU, averages, property sums or histograms, or a custom formula, for one or two events over a date range, optionally segmented and grouped. The main ad-hoc analytics query. Costs rate-limit budget per day, segment and group-by.

event.description: An event definition as a JSON object string, e.g. {"event_type":"Sign Up","filters":[{"subprop_type":"event","subprop_key":"plan","subprop_op":"is","subprop_value":["pro"]}],"group_by":[{"type":"user","value":"platform"}]}. Custom events take a ce: prefix; _active is any active event, _all any event, revenue_amount revenue.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

second_event.description: A second event in the same JSON format, referenced as B in a formula.

metric.description: uniques, totals, pct_dau or average; histogram, sums or value_avg for a property metric (needs a group_by in event); formula for a custom formula (default uniques).

interval.description: -300000 real-time, -3600000 hourly, 1 daily, 7 weekly or 30 monthly (default 1). Real-time covers up to 2 days, hourly up to 7, daily up to 365.

segments.description: Segment definitions as a JSON array string, e.g. [{"prop":"country","op":"is","values":["United States"]}]. Each element has prop, op (is, is not, contains, does not contain, less, less or equal, greater, greater or equal, set is, set is not) and values; use prop "userdata_cohort" with a cohort id to segment by a cohort. Custom user properties are prefixed gp:.

group_by.description: Property to group by, e.g. country, platform or gp:utm_campaign for a custom user property. Only with a single segment.

group_by_2.description: A second property to group by.

limit.description: How many group-by values to return (default 100, maximum 1000).

formula.description: The formula when metric is formula, e.g. UNIQUES(A)/UNIQUES(B).

rolling_window.description: Compute over a rolling window of this many intervals.

rolling_average.description: Compute a rolling average over this many intervals.

output.description: data.series, data.seriesLabels, data.seriesCollapsed and data.xValues.

get_funnel.title: Query a 2-step funnel
get_funnel.description: Run a 2-step funnel analysis: conversion and drop-off per step, cumulative conversion, and median and average transition times, over a date range. Use get_funnel_three_steps, get_funnel_four_steps or get_funnel_five_steps for longer funnels. Costs twice the number of steps per day against the rate limit.
get_funnel.notes: Amplitude reads one `e` query parameter per step, which a query map cannot repeat, so the whole query string travels in the path and segments and group-by are not offered here.

step_1.description: The first funnel step as an event JSON object string. An event definition as a JSON object string, e.g. {"event_type":"Sign Up","filters":[{"subprop_type":"event","subprop_key":"plan","subprop_op":"is","subprop_value":["pro"]}],"group_by":[{"type":"user","value":"platform"}]}. Custom events take a ce: prefix; _active is any active event, _all any event, revenue_amount revenue.

step_2.description: The second funnel step as an event JSON object string.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

mode.description: ordered (steps in order), unordered (any order) or sequential (in order with nothing between).

interval.description: -300000 real-time, -3600000 hourly, 1 daily, 7 weekly or 30 monthly (default 1). Real-time covers up to 2 days, hourly up to 7, daily up to 365.

limit.description: How many group values to return (maximum 1000).

output.description: One element per group with cumulative, cumulativeRaw, stepByStep, medianTransTimes, avgTransTimes, dayFunnels and events.

get_funnel_three_steps.title: Query a 3-step funnel
get_funnel_three_steps.description: Run a 3-step funnel analysis: conversion and drop-off per step, cumulative conversion, and median and average transition times, over a date range. Costs twice the number of steps per day against the rate limit.
get_funnel_three_steps.notes: Amplitude reads one `e` query parameter per step, which a query map cannot repeat, so the whole query string travels in the path and segments and group-by are not offered here.

step_1.description: The first funnel step as an event JSON object string. Custom events take a ce: prefix; _active is any active event, _all any event, revenue_amount revenue.

step_2.description: The second funnel step as an event JSON object string.

step_3.description: The third funnel step as an event JSON object string.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

mode.description: ordered (steps in order), unordered (any order) or sequential (in order with nothing between).

interval.description: -300000 real-time, -3600000 hourly, 1 daily, 7 weekly or 30 monthly (default 1). Real-time covers up to 2 days, hourly up to 7, daily up to 365.

limit.description: How many group values to return (maximum 1000).

output.description: One element per group with cumulative, cumulativeRaw, stepByStep, medianTransTimes, avgTransTimes, dayFunnels and events.

get_funnel_four_steps.description: Run a 4-step funnel analysis: conversion and drop-off per step, cumulative conversion, and median and average transition times, over a date range. Costs twice the number of steps per day against the rate limit.
get_funnel_four_steps.notes: Amplitude reads one `e` query parameter per step, which a query map cannot repeat, so the whole query string travels in the path and segments and group-by are not offered here.

step_1.description: The first funnel step as an event JSON object string. An event definition as a JSON object string, e.g. {"event_type":"Sign Up","filters":[{"subprop_type":"event","subprop_key":"plan","subprop_op":"is","subprop_value":["pro"]}],"group_by":[{"type":"user","value":"platform"}]}. Custom events take a ce: prefix; _active is any active event, _all any event, revenue_amount revenue.

step_2.description: The second funnel step as an event JSON object string.

step_3.description: The third funnel step as an event JSON object string.

step_4.description: The fourth funnel step as an event JSON object string.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

mode.description: ordered (steps in order), unordered (any order) or sequential (in order with nothing between).

interval.description: -300000 real-time, -3600000 hourly, 1 daily, 7 weekly or 30 monthly (default 1). Real-time covers up to 2 days, hourly up to 7, daily up to 365.

output.description: One element per group with cumulative, cumulativeRaw, stepByStep, medianTransTimes, avgTransTimes, dayFunnels and events.

get_funnel_five_steps.description: Run a 5-step funnel analysis: conversion and drop-off per step, cumulative conversion, and median and average transition times, over a date range. Costs twice the number of steps per day against the rate limit.
get_funnel_five_steps.notes: Amplitude reads one `e` query parameter per step, which a query map cannot repeat, so the whole query string travels in the path and segments and group-by are not offered here.

step_1.description: The first funnel step as an event JSON object string. An event definition as a JSON object string, e.g. {"event_type":"Sign Up","filters":[{"subprop_type":"event","subprop_key":"plan","subprop_op":"is","subprop_value":["pro"]}],"group_by":[{"type":"user","value":"platform"}]}. Custom events take a ce: prefix; _active is any active event, _all any event, revenue_amount revenue.

step_2.description: The second funnel step as an event JSON object string.

step_3.description: The third funnel step as an event JSON object string.

step_4.description: The fourth funnel step as an event JSON object string.

step_5.description: The fifth funnel step as an event JSON object string.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

mode.description: ordered (steps in order), unordered (any order) or sequential (in order with nothing between).

interval.description: -300000 real-time, -3600000 hourly, 1 daily, 7 weekly or 30 monthly (default 1). Real-time covers up to 2 days, hourly up to 7, daily up to 365.

limit.description: How many group values to return (maximum 1000).

output.description: One element per group with cumulative, cumulativeRaw, stepByStep, medianTransTimes, avgTransTimes, dayFunnels and events.

get_retention.title: Query retention
get_retention.description: Run a retention analysis: of the users who did a starting event on each date, how many came back to do a returning event N days, weeks or months later. Supports n-day, rolling (unbounded) and bracket retention.

start_event.description: The starting event as an event JSON object string; event_type may be _new for new users or _active for all users, or a real event.

return_event.description: The returning event as an event JSON object string; event_type may be _all or _active, or a real event.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

retention_brackets.description: Brackets when retention_mode is bracket, as a JSON array string, e.g. [[0,5]] for Day 0 to Day 4.

interval.description: 1 for daily, 7 for weekly or 30 for monthly counts (default 1).

segments.description: Segment definitions as a JSON array string, e.g. [{"prop":"country","op":"is","values":["United States"]}]. Each element has prop, op (is, is not, contains, does not contain, less, less or equal, greater, greater or equal, set is, set is not) and values; use prop "userdata_cohort" with a cohort id to segment by a cohort. Custom user properties are prefixed gp:.

group_by.description: Property to group by, e.g. country, platform or gp:utm_campaign for a custom user property. Only with a single segment.

output.description: data.series with dates and values per date cohort (index 0 the cohort size, index N+1 retention after N intervals), plus combined and seriesMeta.

get_user_activity.title: Get a user's activity
get_user_activity.description: Get one user's summary (user properties and totals) and their most recent or earliest events, by Amplitude ID. Find the Amplitude ID with search_users first. Limited to 360 queries an hour.

offset.description: Zero-based offset from the most recent event to start from.

direction.description: latest for the most recent events or earliest for the first ones (default latest).

output.description: events (the user's events) and userData (properties and totals).

search_users.title: Search for a user
search_users.description: Find users by Amplitude ID, device ID, user ID or user ID prefix. Returns the matches' Amplitude IDs and user IDs, which get_user_activity and the privacy tools need.

user.description: An Amplitude ID, device ID, user ID or user ID prefix.

output.description: matches (user_id and amplitude_id each) and type, the kind of match, or nomatch.

get_realtime_active_users.title: Get real-time active users
get_realtime_active_users.description: Get active user counts at 5-minute granularity for today and yesterday.

output.description: data.series for Today and Yesterday, data.xValues with HH:mm times.

get_revenue_ltv.title: Get revenue lifetime value
get_revenue_ltv.description: Get the lifetime value of new users per acquisition date: ARPU, ARPPU, total revenue or paying users, with 1- to 90-day values.

start.description: First date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240101. Dates are in the project's time zone.

end.description: Last date included, formatted YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20240131.

metric.description: 0 average revenue per user, 1 average revenue per paying user, 2 total revenue, 3 paying users (default 0).

interval.description: 1 for daily, 7 for weekly or 30 for monthly counts (default 1).

segments.description: Segment definitions as a JSON array string, e.g. [{"prop":"country","op":"is","values":["United States"]}]. Each element has prop, op (is, is not, contains, does not contain, less, less or equal, greater, greater or equal, set is, set is not) and values; use prop "userdata_cohort" with a cohort id to segment by a cohort. Custom user properties are prefixed gp:.

group_by.description: Property to group by, e.g. country, platform or gp:utm_campaign for a custom user property. Only with a single segment.

output.description: data.series with dates and, per date, r1d..r90d, count, paid and total_amount.

list_cohorts.title: List cohorts
list_cohorts.description: List every discoverable behavioral cohort in the project, with ids, names, sizes, owners and definitions. Cohort ids from here feed request_cohort_download and cohort segments (prop userdata_cohort).

include_sync_info.description: Include each cohort's sync metadata (one-time and disabled syncs are left out).

output.description: cohorts, each with id, name, size, owners, definition and, when asked, syncs.

request_cohort_download.title: Request a cohort download
request_cohort_download.description: Start an asynchronous export of one cohort's members: step one of three. Poll get_cohort_request_status with the returned request_id, then fetch the members with download_cohort_file. Counts toward the 500-a-month download allowance.

cohort_id.description: The cohort id, from list_cohorts or the cohort's URL.

props.description: 1 to include user properties in the export, 0 to leave them out (use 0 if requests time out).

prop_key.description: One user property to include when props is 1; without it every property is included.

output.description: request_id and cohort_id.

get_cohort_request_status.title: Get a cohort download's status
get_cohort_request_status.description: Poll a cohort download started by request_cohort_download. async_status reads JOB INPROGRESS until the file is ready and JOB COMPLETED when download_cohort_file can fetch it.

output.description: request_id, cohort_id and async_status.

download_cohort_file.title: Download a cohort's members
download_cohort_file.description: Fetch the members of a completed cohort download as CSV: step three after request_cohort_download and get_cohort_request_status. Large cohorts redirect to a one-minute S3 link, which is followed. The request link stays valid for seven days.

request_id.description: The request_id returned by request_cohort_download, once its status is JOB COMPLETED.

output.description: The cohort members as CSV text.

get_cohort_download_usage.title: Get cohort download usage
get_cohort_download_usage.description: Check this month's Behavioral Cohorts download usage against its limit (500 a month on Growth and Enterprise) and when it resets.

output.description: rest_download with limit, usage and resets_at.

upload_cohort.title: Create a cohort from ids
upload_cohort.description: Create a new static cohort from a list of user IDs or Amplitude IDs. To overwrite an existing cohort's members use replace_cohort_members; to add or remove a few ids use update_cohort_membership.

app_id.description: The Amplitude project (app) id the cohort belongs to.

id_type.description: What ids holds: Amplitude IDs or user IDs.

ids.description: The Amplitude IDs or user IDs that make up the cohort (up to 100,000).

owner.description: Login email of the cohort's owner in Amplitude.

published.description: true to make the cohort discoverable, false to keep it hidden.

count_group.description: An existing group type to base the cohort on, instead of users.

skip_save.description: Validate the upload without saving it.

skip_invalid_ids.description: Skip invalid ids and upload the rest, rather than failing (default true).

output.description: cohortId and metadata with matched, totals and invalid_ids_sample.

replace_cohort_members.title: Replace a cohort's members
replace_cohort_members.description: Replace every member of an existing cohort with a new list of user IDs or Amplitude IDs. The previous membership is gone; use update_cohort_membership to add or remove ids incrementally.

app_id.description: The Amplitude project (app) id the cohort belongs to.

id_type.description: What ids holds: Amplitude IDs or user IDs.

ids.description: The Amplitude IDs or user IDs that make up the cohort (up to 100,000).

owner.description: Login email of the cohort's owner in Amplitude.

published.description: true to make the cohort discoverable, false to keep it hidden.

count_group.description: An existing group type to base the cohort on, instead of users.

skip_save.description: Validate the upload without saving it.

skip_invalid_ids.description: Skip invalid ids and upload the rest, rather than failing (default true).

existing_cohort_id.description: The id of the cohort whose members are replaced.

output.description: cohortId and metadata with matched, totals and invalid_ids_sample.

update_cohort_membership.title: Add or remove cohort members
update_cohort_membership.description: Add ids to, or remove ids from, an existing cohort without replacing it. BY_ID means Amplitude IDs (group ids for group cohorts), BY_NAME means user IDs (group names).

cohort_id.description: The id of the cohort to change.

operation.description: Whether to add or remove the ids.

id_type.description: BY_ID for Amplitude IDs or group ids, BY_NAME for user IDs or group names.

ids.description: The ids to add or remove.

count_group.description: The cohort's count group; must match the cohort (default User).

skip_invalid_ids.description: Skip invalid ids rather than failing the whole request (default true).

output.description: cohort_id and memberships_result with skipped_ids per operation.

list_event_categories.title: List event categories
list_event_categories.description: List the tracking plan's event categories with their ids and names.

output.description: success and data, the categories with id and name.

get_event_category.title: Get an event category
get_event_category.description: Get one tracking-plan event category, including its id, by name.

output.description: success and data with the category's id and name.

create_event_category.title: Create an event category
create_event_category.description: Create an event category in the tracking plan, for grouping event types.

output.description: success, or an error when the category exists.

update_event_category.title: Rename an event category
update_event_category.description: Rename a tracking-plan event category, by its id (see list_event_categories).

output.description: success, or an error on a conflict.

delete_event_category.title: Delete an event category
delete_event_category.description: Delete a tracking-plan event category by id. Event types in it become uncategorized.

output.description: success, or an error.

list_event_types.title: List tracking-plan event types
list_event_types.description: List every event type in the tracking plan with category, description, visibility flags, tags and owner. Hidden events are left out; set show_deleted to include deleted ones. For weekly volumes use list_events.

output.description: success and data, the event types.

get_event_type.title: Get an event type
get_event_type.description: Get one tracking-plan event type by name, with its category, description, flags and owner.

output.description: success and data with the event type.

create_event_type.title: Create an event type
create_event_type.description: Add a planned event type to the tracking plan, with an optional category, description, visibility flags, tags and owner.

description.description: What the event means and when it fires.

is_active.description: Whether the event type is active.

is_hidden_from_dropdowns.description: Hide the event from chart dropdowns.

is_hidden_from_persona_results.description: Hide the event from persona results.

is_hidden_from_timeline.description: Hide the event from user timelines.

output.description: success, or an error when the event type exists.

update_event_type.title: Update an event type
update_event_type.description: Update a tracking-plan event type: rename it, set its display name, category, description, visibility flags, tags or owner. Only the fields given change.

new_event_type.description: A new name for the event type.

display_name.description: Display name for an ingested event type.

description.description: What the event means and when it fires.

is_active.description: Whether the event type is active.

is_hidden_from_dropdowns.description: Hide the event from chart dropdowns.

is_hidden_from_persona_results.description: Hide the event from persona results.

is_hidden_from_timeline.description: Hide the event from user timelines.

output.description: success, or an error on a conflict.

delete_event_type.title: Delete an event type
delete_event_type.description: Delete an event type from the tracking plan. A live event is marked deleted (restore_event_type undoes it), an unexpected one is added then marked deleted, and a planned one is removed outright.

output.description: success, or an error.

restore_event_type.title: Restore a deleted event type
restore_event_type.description: Restore an event type that was marked deleted, resuming its ingestion.

output.description: success, or an error when the event is not deleted or not found.

list_event_properties.title: List event properties
list_event_properties.description: List the event properties of one event type, or every shared event property in the tracking plan when event_type is omitted.
list_event_properties.notes: Amplitude documents event_type as a body field on this GET; it is sent as a query parameter.

event_type.description: The event type whose properties to list; omit for all shared properties.

output.description: success and data, the event properties.

get_event_property.title: Get an event property
get_event_property.description: Get one event property by name, either the shared definition or the one on a given event type.
get_event_property.notes: Amplitude documents event_type as a body field on this GET; it is sent as a query parameter.

event_type.description: The event type whose version of the property to read.

output.description: success and data with the property.

create_event_property.title: Create an event property
create_event_property.description: Create an event property in the tracking plan, optionally on an event type, with type, validation, visibility and classification settings.

event_type.description: The event type to attach the property to. When the property exists elsewhere, an override is created for this event.

is_required.description: Mark the property required on the event.

regex.description: A pattern string values must match, e.g. [0-9]{5}. Only for the string type.

enum_values.description: Allowed values, comma-separated, e.g. red, yellow, blue. Only for the enum type.

is_array_type.description: Whether the value is an array; type sets the element type.

is_hidden.description: Hide the property from chart dropdowns.

classifications.description: Data classifications, comma-separated: PII, SENSITIVE, REVENUE. Shared properties only; needs Data Access Controls.

output.description: success, or an error when the property already exists on that event.

update_event_property.title: Update an event property
update_event_property.description: Update an event property's name, description, type, validation, visibility or classifications, either shared or on one event type.

event_type.description: The event type whose version to update.

override_scope.description: With event_type: override to create or update an event-level override, shared to drop the override and update the shared property.

new_event_property_value.description: A new name for the property.

is_required.description: Mark the property required on the event.

regex.description: A pattern string values must match, e.g. [0-9]{5}. Only for the string type.

enum_values.description: Allowed values, comma-separated, e.g. red, yellow, blue. Only for the enum type.

is_array_type.description: Whether the value is an array; type sets the element type.

is_hidden.description: Hide the property from chart dropdowns.

classifications.description: Data classifications, comma-separated: PII, SENSITIVE, REVENUE. Shared properties only; needs Data Access Controls.

output.description: success, or an error on a conflict.

delete_event_property.title: Delete an event property
delete_event_property.description: Delete an event property. With event_type it is only removed from that event; without, a live property is marked deleted, an unexpected one added then marked deleted, and a planned one removed.

event_type.description: Only remove the property from this event type.

output.description: success, or an error.

restore_event_property.title: Restore a deleted event property
restore_event_property.description: Restore an event property that was marked deleted, shared or on one event type.

event_type.description: Restore it on this event type only; omit for the shared property.

output.description: success, or an error.

list_user_properties.title: List user properties
list_user_properties.description: List every user property in the tracking plan, with type, description and flags. Set show_deleted to include deleted ones.

output.description: success and data, the user properties.

get_user_property.title: Get a user property
get_user_property.description: Get one user property by name, with its type, description and flags.

user_property.description: The user property's name; custom user properties take a gp: prefix, e.g. gp:plan.

show_deleted.description: Return the property even if it is deleted.

output.description: success and data with the user property.

create_user_property.title: Create a user property
create_user_property.description: Add a user property to the tracking plan with its type, validation, visibility and classifications.

user_property.description: Name of the new user property.

regex.description: A pattern string values must match, e.g. [0-9]{5}. Only for the string type.

enum_values.description: Allowed values, comma-separated, e.g. red, yellow, blue. Only for the enum type.

is_array_type.description: Whether the value is an array; type sets the element type.

is_hidden.description: Hide the property from chart dropdowns.

classifications.description: Data classifications, comma-separated: PII, SENSITIVE, REVENUE. Shared properties only; needs Data Access Controls.

output.description: success, or an error.

update_user_property.title: Update a user property
update_user_property.description: Update a user property's name, description, type, validation, visibility or classifications.

user_property.description: The user property's name; custom user properties take a gp: prefix, e.g. gp:plan.

new_user_property_value.description: A new name for the user property.

regex.description: A pattern string values must match, e.g. [0-9]{5}. Only for the string type.

enum_values.description: Allowed values, comma-separated, e.g. red, yellow, blue. Only for the enum type.

is_array_type.description: Whether the value is an array; type sets the element type.

is_hidden.description: Hide the property from chart dropdowns.

classifications.description: Data classifications, comma-separated: PII, SENSITIVE, REVENUE. Shared properties only; needs Data Access Controls.

output.description: success, or an error.

delete_user_property.title: Delete a user property
delete_user_property.description: Delete a user property from the tracking plan: a live one is marked deleted (restore_user_property undoes it), a planned one removed. Amplitude's own user properties cannot be deleted.

user_property.description: The user property's name; custom user properties take a gp: prefix, e.g. gp:plan.

output.description: success, or an error.

restore_user_property.title: Restore a deleted user property
restore_user_property.description: Restore a user property that was marked deleted.

user_property.description: The user property's name; custom user properties take a gp: prefix, e.g. gp:plan.

output.description: success, or an error when it is not deleted or not found.

list_group_properties.title: List group properties
list_group_properties.description: List the group properties of one group type, or every shared group property when group_type is omitted.

group_type.description: The group type whose properties to list.

output.description: success and data, the group properties.

get_group_property.title: Get a group property
get_group_property.description: Get one group property by name, shared or on a given group type.

group_property.description: The group property's name; custom group properties take a grp: prefix.

group_type.description: The group type whose version to read.

output.description: success and data with the group property.

create_group_property.title: Create a group property
create_group_property.description: Add a group property to the tracking plan, optionally on a group type, with type, validation, visibility and classifications.

group_property.description: The group property's name; custom group properties take a grp: prefix.

group_type.description: The group type to attach the property to; creates an override when it exists elsewhere.

regex.description: A pattern string values must match, e.g. [0-9]{5}. Only for the string type.

enum_values.description: Allowed values, comma-separated, e.g. red, yellow, blue. Only for the enum type.

is_array_type.description: Whether the value is an array; type sets the element type.

is_hidden.description: Hide the property from chart dropdowns.

classifications.description: Data classifications, comma-separated: PII, SENSITIVE, REVENUE. Shared properties only; needs Data Access Controls.

output.description: success, or an error when it already exists.

update_group_property.title: Update a group property
update_group_property.description: Update a custom group property's name, description, type, validation, visibility or classifications. Amplitude-sourced group properties cannot be edited.

group_property.description: The group property's name; custom group properties take a grp: prefix.

group_type.description: The group type whose version to update.

override_scope.description: With group_type: override to create or update a group-type override, shared to drop it and update the shared property.

new_group_property_value.description: A new name for the group property.

regex.description: A pattern string values must match, e.g. [0-9]{5}. Only for the string type.

enum_values.description: Allowed values, comma-separated, e.g. red, yellow, blue. Only for the enum type.

is_array_type.description: Whether the value is an array; type sets the element type.

is_hidden.description: Hide the property from chart dropdowns.

classifications.description: Data classifications, comma-separated: PII, SENSITIVE, REVENUE. Shared properties only; needs Data Access Controls.

output.description: success, or an error on a conflict.

list_annotation_categories.title: List annotation categories
list_annotation_categories.description: List chart annotation categories, or just the one named in category.

category.description: Only return the category with this name.

output.description: The annotation categories with id and category.

get_annotation_category.title: Get an annotation category
get_annotation_category.description: Get one chart annotation category by its id.

output.description: The category with id and category.

create_annotation_category.title: Create an annotation category
create_annotation_category.description: Create a category for grouping chart annotations.

output.description: The new category with its id.

update_annotation_category.title: Rename an annotation category
update_annotation_category.description: Rename a chart annotation category, keeping its id and annotations.

output.description: The updated category.

delete_annotation_category.title: Delete an annotation category
delete_annotation_category.description: Delete a chart annotation category by id.

output.description: Confirmation of the deletion.

assign_annotations_to_category.title: Move annotations into a category
assign_annotations_to_category.description: Assign several chart annotations to one category at once.

category_id.description: The category to assign them to.

annotation_ids.description: Ids of the annotations to move.

output.description: The result of the bulk update.

list_annotations.title: List chart annotations
list_annotations.description: List chart annotations, filtered by category or by chart (not both), and by a start and end time.

chart_id.description: Only annotations shown on this chart.

start.description: Only annotations after this ISO 8601 time, e.g. 2025-11-01T07:00:00+00:00.

end.description: Only annotations ending before this ISO 8601 time.

output.description: The annotations with id, label, details, start, end, category and chart_id.

get_annotation.title: Get a chart annotation
get_annotation.description: Get one chart annotation by its id, with its label, times, category and chart.

output.description: The annotation.

create_annotation.title: Create a chart annotation
create_annotation.description: Mark a moment or a time range on charts, such as a launch, incident or campaign, globally or on a single chart.

end.description: End time in ISO 8601, for an annotation that spans a range.

category.description: Name of the category the annotation belongs to.

chart_id.description: Pin the annotation to this chart; without it the annotation shows on every chart.

output.description: The new annotation with its id.

update_annotation.title: Update a chart annotation
update_annotation.description: Change a chart annotation's label, times, category, chart or details. Only the fields given change.

end.description: End time in ISO 8601, for an annotation that spans a range.

category.description: Name of the category the annotation belongs to.

chart_id.description: Pin the annotation to this chart; without it the annotation shows on every chart.

output.description: The updated annotation.

delete_annotation.title: Delete a chart annotation
delete_annotation.description: Delete a chart annotation by id; it disappears from every chart it showed on.

output.description: Confirmation of the deletion.

create_release.title: Create a release
create_release.description: Record a product release so it appears on charts as an annotation, with version, title, start and optional end, platforms and description.

version.description: The product version this release corresponds to, e.g. 3.5.

release_start.description: Release start in UTC, formatted yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.

release_end.description: Release end in UTC, formatted yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.

platforms.description: The platforms the release covers, e.g. iOS.

created_by.description: Name of the person creating the release.

chart_visibility.description: Show the release on charts as an annotation (default true).

output.description: The created release.

request_user_deletion.title: Delete users' data
request_user_deletion.description: Schedule users' data for permanent deletion by Amplitude ID and/or user ID, from this project or, with delete_from_org, from every project in the organization. Deletion jobs start after a delay during which remove_user_from_deletion_job can take a user back out.

amplitude_ids.description: Amplitude IDs of the users to delete.

user_ids.description: User IDs of the users to delete.

requester.description: Who asked for the deletion, for auditing.

ignore_invalid_id.description: Skip users with no data here instead of failing the whole request.

delete_from_org.description: Delete the users from every project in the organization.

include_mapped_user_ids.description: Return the user_id matching each supplied amplitude_id.

output.description: The deletion job: day, status, amplitude_ids and user_ids, and invalid_ids when skipped.

list_deletion_jobs.title: List deletion jobs
list_deletion_jobs.description: List user-deletion jobs scheduled between two days, with the users in each and who requested them.

output.description: The deletion jobs with day, status and amplitude_ids.

remove_user_from_deletion_job.title: Remove a user from a deletion job
remove_user_from_deletion_job.description: Take one user back out of a scheduled deletion job before it runs.

amplitude_id.description: The Amplitude ID to remove from the job.

job_start_day.description: The day the job is scheduled for, YYYY-MM-DD.

output.description: The removed user's amplitude_id, requester and requested_on_day.

map_user.title: Map a user ID to a global user
map_user.description: Alias one user ID to a global user ID, so events from both appear on the global user. User properties are not merged. Use map_users for many mappings in one call and unmap_user to undo.
map_user.notes: The Aliasing API takes the project API key as a query parameter; it is read from the connection's credentials. It runs on api.amplitude.com, so EU projects are not served.

global_user_id.description: The global user ID to map it into.

output.description: The Aliasing API's acknowledgement.

unmap_user.title: Remove a user's mapping
unmap_user.description: Remove the current mapping of a user ID to its global user ID.
unmap_user.notes: The Aliasing API takes the project API key as a query parameter; it is read from the connection's credentials. It runs on api.amplitude.com, so EU projects are not served.

output.description: The Aliasing API's acknowledgement.

map_users.title: Map or unmap user IDs in bulk
map_users.description: Apply up to 2000 alias mappings in one call. Each object maps a user_id to a global_user_id, or sets unmap to true to remove the user_id's mapping.
map_users.notes: The Aliasing API takes the project API key as a query parameter; it is read from the connection's credentials. It runs on api.amplitude.com, so EU projects are not served.

mapping.description: The mappings as a JSON array string, e.g. [{"user_id":"a@x.com","global_user_id":"hank@y.net"},{"user_id":"b@x.com","unmap":true}].

output.description: The Aliasing API's acknowledgement.

get_user_mappings.title: Get users' mappings
get_user_mappings.description: Get the mappings that involve a user ID: which users map into it and what it maps into, with Amplitude IDs.
get_user_mappings.notes: Amplitude accepts up to 100 user ids; this tool looks up one per call.

user_id.description: The user ID to look up.

output.description: Per user id, its mappings with amplitude_id, mapped_from and mapped_to.

send_attribution_event.title: Send an attribution event
send_attribution_event.description: Send a mobile attribution event (e.g. [YOUR COMPANY] Install) matched to users by advertising id. Amplitude holds it up to 72 hours for a matching user, then applies its user_properties. Ingested data cannot be recalled.
send_attribution_event.notes: The Attribution API takes the project API key as a query parameter; it is read from the connection's credentials. It runs on api.amplitude.com, so EU projects are not served.

event.description: The event as a JSON object string with event_type, platform (ios or android), idfa or idfv on iOS, adid or android_app_set_id on Android, optional user_properties and time, e.g. {"event_type":"[Acme] Install","platform":"ios","idfa":"AEBE52E7-...","user_properties":{"[Acme] media source":"facebook"}}.

output.description: Success, or a 400 when the JSON is malformed.

ingest_feedback.title: Send customer feedback
ingest_feedback.description: Send 1-100 customer feedback items (NPS answers, reviews, tickets with replies, call transcripts) to an AI Feedback webhook source. Items and conversation parts are upserted by unique_id, so re-sending is safe.
ingest_feedback.notes: EU projects use eu.amplitude.com for this endpoint, which the connection's analytics.eu.amplitude.com base does not reach.

source_id.description: The webhook source's id, from the source's Settings in AI Feedback.

items.description: Feedback items: unique_id (required), body, author, email, user_id, url, created_at, and conversation_parts (same fields, body required).

output.description: ingested, failed and errors per unique_id.
